material_declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.pi
material_declarations.meaning: The product law multiplies probabilities on cylinders indexed by the finitely many unordered edges.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The construction passes through the product outer measure and the Caratheodory measurable sets. The cylinder identity is a proved characterization.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure
material_declarations.meaning: For distinct outcomes 1 and 0, the two masses are the given edge probability and its complement.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Unit-interval weights scale the two Dirac measures. The pinned real-application lemma specifies their contributions on measurable sets.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
material_declarations.meaning: The conclusion compares the real-valued probability of a failure event to a real bound.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The measure is evaluated in the extended nonnegative reals, then converted by toReal. Finite Bernoulli product probability laws give finite event masses.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Set.Icc
material_declarations.meaning: The probability and kernel-coordinate types use the closed interval including both endpoints.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: Membership expands to the conjunction of the lower and upper order inequalities. Subtype projection returns the real value.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Set.iUnion
material_declarations.meaning: The graph event asserts the existence of an induced subset of the permitted order.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The set supremum over the family has existential membership, indexed by finite vertex subsets satisfying the order predicate.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Set.preimage
material_declarations.meaning: The induced regularity event pulls the local degree condition back to the ambient graph outcomes.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: A graph is in the preimage exactly when its restriction to edges of the given vertex set satisfies the local regularity condition.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Set.compl
material_declarations.meaning: The bounds are for the failure of the stated existence events.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The notation `sᶜ` uses the `Compl (Set α)` instance in `Operations.lean`. Its body is definitionally equal to `Set.compl`. `Set.mem_compl_iff` gives negated membership in the corresponding exact-order or at-least-order event.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Nat.ceil
material_declarations.meaning: The logarithmic thresholds round up to a natural order.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The FloorSemiring ceiling has the Galois connection with natural-number coercion. A natural order meets the ceiling exactly when its real value meets the unrounded threshold.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Finset.card
material_declarations.meaning: The vertex order counts the elements of a finite subset.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The finite set has an underlying duplicate-free multiset. Its multiset cardinality agrees with the usual count.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.rpow
material_declarations.meaning: The structural order thresholds and failure exponents use ordinary positive-base real powers.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition takes the real part of a complex power. For a positive base, the checked contract identifies it with the exponential of the logarithm times the exponent.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.log
material_declarations.meaning: The thresholds in the arbitrary-array bounds use the natural logarithm.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The positive-real branch is inverse to the real exponential. The ordinary square is a natural power of the logarithm.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.exp
material_declarations.meaning: The failure bounds use the usual natural exponential.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition takes the real part of the complex exponential on the real axis. The complex exponential is defined by its convergent power series.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Real.sqrt
material_declarations.meaning: The amplified logarithmic bound uses the nonnegative square root of the number of vertices.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition applies NNReal.sqrt to the nonnegative part. The checked Real.sqrt_eq_rpow contract identifies the root with the one-half power.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Matrix.rank
material_declarations.meaning: The rank cap is the rank of the real matrix that completes the edge array.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition is the natural dimension of the range of the matrix-vector linear map. Over the real field with finite indices this is the usual column rank.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

material_declarations.name: Module.finrank
material_declarations.meaning: Finite real vector-space dimension is a natural number.
material_declarations.dependency_expansion: The definition uses the natural value of the cardinal-valued module rank. Subspaces of the finite-dimensional codomain in the completion hypothesis have finite rank.
material_declarations.proof_status: See the separate ChallengeSemantics and SolutionSemantics entrypoints.

excerpts.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.pi.definition
excerpts.text:
protected irreducible_def pi : Measure (∀ i, α i) :=
  toMeasure (OuterMeasure.pi fun i => (μ i).toOuterMeasure) (pi_caratheodory μ)

excerpts.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.pi.contract
excerpts.text:
theorem pi_pi [∀ i, SigmaFinite (μ i)] (s : (i : ι) → Set (α i)) :
    Measure.pi μ (pi univ s) = ∏ i, μ i (s i) := by
  have : Encodable ι := Fintype.toEncodable ι
  rw [← pi'_eq_pi, pi'_pi]

excerpts.name: ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure.definition
excerpts.text:
noncomputable def bernoulliMeasure (x y : X) (p : I) : Measure X :=
  toNNReal p • dirac x + toNNReal (σ p) • dirac y

excerpts.name: ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure.contract
excerpts.text:
lemma bernoulliMeasure_real_apply (p : I) {s : Set X}
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) [DecidablePred (· ∈ s)] :
    Ber(x, y, p).real s =
      if x ∈ s
        then if y ∈ s
          then (1 : ℝ)
          else toNNReal p
        else if y ∈ s
          then toNNReal (σ p)
          else 0 := by
  simp [measureReal_def, bernoulliMeasure_apply p hs, apply_ite ENNReal.toReal]
